name: gizza-ai/dbf-table-parser
summary: Parse a dBase/.dbf table file into columns and rows (CSV or JSON)

tool.description: Parse a dBase / .dbf table file into its column definitions and rows, exportable as CSV or JSON. Provide the file via `url` (a public http/https link) or `ref` (an uploaded attachment id). Reads dBase III/IV and FoxPro DBFs: field types C (character), N/F (numeric), D (date → YYYY-MM-DD), L (logical → true/false), and I (4-byte integer); memo (M) cells emit empty because the sidecar .dbt/.fpt file isn't available to a single-file tool. Options: `format` (csv default, or json with typed cells + column defs), `delimiter` (csv; single char or "tab"), `header` (csv), `columns` (keep/reorder a subset by name or 0-based index), `include_deleted` (default false), `trim` (default true), `encoding` (auto/utf-8/latin1/cp1252), and `limit` (row cap for previews).

columns.description: Comma-separated columns to keep and reorder, by name (case-insensitive) or 0-based index, e.g. "NAME,2,PRICE". Leave empty to keep every column in file order.

delimiter.description: CSV field separator: a single character, or the word "tab" for a tab. Ignored for JSON. Defaults to a comma.

encoding.description: Text decoding for character fields. "auto" uses UTF-8 when valid else Latin-1; "latin1" (ISO-8859-1) and "cp1252" (Windows-1252) cover most legacy DBFs. Defaults to auto.

format.description: Output format. "csv" writes the table as delimited text (header row + rows). "json" writes {columns:[{name,type,length,decimal}], row_count, rows:[{col:value}]} with numeric/logical/date cells typed. Defaults to csv.

header.description: Write a first CSV row of column names. Set false to omit it. Ignored for JSON. Defaults to true.

include_deleted.description: Include records flagged as deleted in the .dbf (marked with a leading '*'). Defaults to false (skips them, like most viewers).

limit.description: Maximum number of data rows to output; 0 (the default) writes every row. Use a small value to preview a large table.

ref.description: Reference id from a prior tool call. Use either url or ref.

trim.description: Trim trailing padding spaces from fixed-width character fields. Set false to keep the original padding. Defaults to true.

url.description: File URL (HTTP/HTTPS). Use either url or ref.
